altitudes.name: The 12,000
altitudes.tagline: 12,000 feet. Up to 45 seconds of freefall. One hell of a way to see Canterbury.
altitudes.headline: The altitude changes everything.
story: 12,000 feet above Canterbury, the ground starts to feel a long way away. Christchurch, the Southern Alps, Banks Peninsula and the Canterbury Plains stretch out beneath you, while the aircraft door becomes your only reference point.
200 km/h. Nothing between you and the sky. Just open air and a perspective that can't be replicated from the ground.
This is the full DropX experience. Big altitude. Big freefall. One unforgettable view.
12,000 feet above Canterbury. Then there's nowhere left to go, but out.

altitudes.name: The 9,000
altitudes.tagline: 9,000 feet. Pure freefall. A serious introduction to skydiving.
altitudes.headline: Closer to the ground. No less of an experience.
story: At 9,000 feet, you're high enough to see Canterbury unfold beneath you, but close enough to appreciate just how fast the ground is coming towards you.
The aircraft climbs. The anticipation builds. Then the door opens.
Step into the sky and experience freefall at 200 km/h, before the parachute opens and the noise gives way to a completely different kind of silence.

items: Ground briefing with your tandem instructor

items.label: Age
items.detail: Under 18s need a parent or guardian to sign on the day.

items.label: Weight
items.detail: Over 95kg? Call us before you book so we can match you with the right instructor.

items.label: Health
items.detail: Let us know about any medical conditions, recent injuries, or pregnancy before you book.

items.label: Shoes
items.detail: Closed shoes that stay on. No boots, sandals or jandals.

day.duration: Allow about 3 hours at the drop zone

steps.title: Check in
steps.body: Arrive at the drop zone, sign your forms and meet your instructor.
steps.alt: Tandem instructor and customer with hand signals on the landing field

steps.title: Gear up
steps.body: Get fitted in your harness and run through the briefing on the ground. It takes about 20 minutes.
steps.alt: Tandem pair leaving the aircraft under the wing

steps.title: Freefall
steps.body: Climb to altitude, exit the aircraft and fall at around 200km/h with the plains and coast below you.
steps.alt: Smiling tandem customer in freefall above the Canterbury hills

steps.title: Land
steps.body: Your instructor opens the parachute and flies you back to the field. You can help steer.
steps.alt: Tandem customer walking back in from the landing area with the instructor

location.directions: Directions and parking details to confirm.
location.spectators: Friends and family are welcome to come and watch the landings.

media.intro: The skydive is over in minutes. The memory isn't.
media.delivery: Photos and edited video are sent to you by download link after your jump.
media.own_camera: For safety, you can't take your own phone, GoPro or camera on the jump. Our camera packages are the only way to get footage from the air.

view.headline: Some views are earned.
story: From the ground, Canterbury is beautiful.
From 12,000 feet, it becomes something else entirely.
The Southern Alps. The plains. The coastline. Christchurch.
All from a perspective you can't reach without leaving the ground.
